security_audit.summary: Two findings are confirmed because the skill instructs agents to run Python crawler and link-analysis helpers. All other findings are Markdown formatting, relative documentation links, diagrams, or repository metadata. No prompt injection or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: Crawler commands start external processes and access a user-supplied URL.
remediation.suggestion: Require confirmation, validate schemes and hosts, block private addresses, and pass URLs as isolated arguments without shell interpolation.

content.user_title: Optimize Your Site Structure and Internal Links
content.value_statement: Complex websites hide important pages and weaken navigation. This skill creates a clear hierarchy, URL plan, link map, and prioritized implementation roadmap.
actual_capabilities: Selects architecture or linking mode from the request.
Designs page hierarchies, navigation zones, and URL taxonomies.
Maps hub-and-spoke topic clusters and cross-section links.
Identifies orphan pages, link islands, crawl-depth issues, and anchor-text problems.
Produces Mermaid site maps, structure scores, redirect guidance, and prioritized action plans.
limitations: Requires a domain, sitemap, page inventory, or user-provided site details.
Cannot measure live metrics without connected crawler, SEO, or analytics tools.
Does not analyze external backlinks, XML sitemap health, or indexation.
Recommendations need human review before URL changes, redirects, deletion, or noindex actions.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Website
use_cases.description: Create a page hierarchy, navigation model, URL taxonomy, and topic clusters before development begins.

use_cases.title: Restructure a Growing Site
use_cases.description: Find buried pages, inconsistent URL parents, weak navigation, and migration risks across an established website.

use_cases.title: Improve Internal Links
use_cases.description: Identify orphans, weak authority flow, generic anchors, and specific source-to-target link opportunities.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Site Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new website
prompt_templates.prompt: Use architecture mode for a new [site type] website. Organize these pages: [page list]. Propose hierarchy, navigation, URLs, and topic clusters.

prompt_templates.title: Restructure an Existing Site
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this sitemap or page inventory: [pages]. Preserve these URLs: [URLs]. Design a clearer structure and include redirects for changed URLs.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Internal Linking
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced analysis of an existing website
prompt_templates.prompt: Use linking mode for [domain or sitemap]. Identify orphans, deep pages, link islands, anchor issues, and prioritized source-target-anchor recommendations.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Controlled Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a phased migration from [current model] to [target model]. Include URL mapping, redirects, navigation changes, link updates, risks, metrics, and validation gates.

output_examples.input: Plan the architecture for a SaaS site with product, pricing, use-case, customer, and resource pages.
output: Architecture mode selected with a shallow SaaS hierarchy.
The plan groups features and use cases under stable parent sections.
Navigation, URL mapping, topic clusters, site map, score, and phased actions are included.

output_examples.input: Find internal linking problems in a content site with a sitemap and crawl export.
output: The audit lists measured orphan pages, deep pages, and under-linked priorities.
Each recommended link includes its source, target, anchor, reason, and priority.
The result includes an anchor review, structure score, and tracking plan.

output_examples.input: Add internal links for a new article about email marketing best practices.
output: The plan connects the article to list building, segmentation, automation, subject lines, and tools pages.
Each spoke receives a descriptive return link to the main article.
Low-value orphan pages receive a review recommendation before redirect or removal.

best_practices: Provide a complete page inventory and mark the most important pages.
Separate measured data, user-provided facts, and estimates.
Review traffic and rankings before deleting, redirecting, or hiding orphan pages.
anti_patterns: Do not change live URLs without a complete redirect map.
Do not treat estimated crawl or link metrics as measured results.
Do not add links only to meet a quota when topics are unrelated.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the site type, goals, page inventory or sitemap, priority pages, audiences, and URLs that must remain unchanged.

faq.question: Can it crawl my website?
faq.answer: It can use a connected crawler with your approval. Without one, it works from a sitemap, export, or page list.

faq.question: What is the difference between the two modes?
faq.answer: Architecture mode designs the website layout. Linking mode improves connections among pages that already exist.

faq.question: Does it create an XML sitemap?
faq.answer: No. It creates visual site maps and URL plans, while XML sitemap and indexation checks require technical SEO tooling.

faq.question: How does it handle orphan pages?
faq.answer: It identifies each orphan, estimates its value, and recommends adding links, redirecting, applying noindex, or removing it after review.

faq.question: Will it change my website automatically?
faq.answer: No. It produces recommendations and implementation plans. A person should approve navigation, URL, redirect, deletion, and noindex changes.
